seo_title: Andrew Forte and Justin on Robinhood Q3 and Serial Deployers
meta_description: Andrew Forte and Justin debate serial token deployers, launchpad incentives and pump.fun's model, and what Robinhood's Q3 call means for Robinhood Chain.
summary: Chill Pill and R2D2 open with Stanley Druckenmiller's first post on X, about Hyperliquid, and a heated debate on serial token deployers and whether anyone will face consequences. Andrew Forte and Justin then discuss how launchpad incentives shape the trenches, what Robinhood's Q3 earnings call said about the chain, and what it costs to build a sustainable crypto business.
takeaways: The hosts read a first post on X about Hyperliquid from TradFi investor Stanley Druckenmiller as a sign that perpetual futures onchain are reaching fund managers and family offices.

Data shared on the stream about October token launches showed a small number of serial deployers launching huge numbers of tokens, with very few graduating; the guests and hosts disagree on whether this will ever be prosecuted.
The guests argue launchpad design drives behaviour: rewarding rotation and call-outs favours deployers who extract the most, which they see as harmful to traders and to the wider market.
On Robinhood's Q3 call, Vlad described the chain's growth and said Robinhood is building a team for it; Justin thinks Robinhood did not expect this level of success and is now catching up.

The guests argue that bootstrapping liquidity and building a sustainable crypto business is expensive, and the closing discussion frames fairer launches as reducing the power the deployer has over traders.
